narration: SKYSHIFT is Project Mercury Team's independent local application for exploring real Sphere X infrared observations. It runs on your Windows computer at localhost, port three thousand, without ChatGPT Sites. This release update uses official mission imagery, actual scientific products and screenshots of the locally running application. A generic computer voice provides the narration. Scientific approval and independent human technical review remain pending.

Sphere X maps the infrared sky across one hundred and two spectral channels. This published NASA composite combines observations and uses selected colors to represent infrared light. It is educational imagery, separate from Skyshift's scientific arrays. Our application offers three curated fields, rather than claiming every sky position or date is available.

The explorer contains four real individual exposures across M one oh one, the M sixty seven outskirts, and the N G C one eighty eight region. Larger contexts provide more space for inspection. Each view preserves its exact date, detector, spectral calibration, original source and hashes. Brightness stretches and single band false colors change presentation. Smooth interpolation adds no measured detail.

Temporal comparison remains restricted to a small M one oh one field. Larger regions failed the unchanged wavelength requirement. The review grid has twenty four by twenty four prepared pixels, with ninety four point four four percent common support. Thirteen independently fitted Gaia references give a median inter epoch residual of about zero point three one arcseconds. These checks do not establish absolute precision or confirm astronomical change.

The audit downloaded both original cutouts and both calibration files again. All four hashes matched. All ten browser arrays matched the prepared FITS and a fresh reconstruction exactly. Ninety two Python tests and twenty eight JavaScript tests pass. Seventeen independent local Chromium checks also pass. They test actual browser exports, reopening, reduced motion, mobile layouts and integrity failures, with no external runtime requests.

This is the actual local exploration workspace. Two individual exposure dates are available for the M one oh one context. Dates, wavelength information and original source identities remain visible. Dark blue areas are masked or unsupported data. This larger context is for individual exposure inspection. The temporal comparison has its own smaller field and separate suitability checks.

The browser saved and reopened this explicitly labeled quality assurance note. The log display, ice palette, prepared pixel sampling and wipe position restored correctly. Offline reconstruction of the actual browser export recovered all ten scientific arrays with zero error. The complete review packet downloaded through the browser with its original exact hash. The pictured note is a software control, not an astronomical finding.

Double click start underscore skyshift dot bat, then keep the server window open. Stop with control C or the stop script. Restart using the startup script. Curated viewing and evidence tools use local assets. New archive retrieval needs internet access. Broader browser and physical device testing, an independent human technical review, qualified astronomical assessment and novice usability sessions remain open. No reviewer approval or discovery has been fabricated.
